entries.title: Media agent outage: every job on one media agent failed
entries.symptoms: All jobs that write through one media agent fail in the same window, across unrelated clients.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: Media agent host is down, rebooting or hung
Backup services stopped on the media agent
Network path or firewall change between clients and the media agent
Disk library mount or storage unreachable
checks: Check whether the media agent host is up and its backup services are running
Check whether the disk library mount path is online and has free space
Confirm whether other media agents at the same site are healthy to separate a host problem from a site problem
fixes: Restore the host or services, then rerun the failed jobs
If the host cannot be recovered quickly, redirect affected clients to another media agent and escalate

entries.title: Repeat failure: same client failed several nights in a row
entries.symptoms: One client fails on consecutive nights with the same error, so a retry is not fixing it.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: A persistent client-side problem (agent, snapshot, credentials) that a retry does not clear
A configuration change made before the first failure
A chain or dependency broken until a fresh full backup runs
checks: Compare the error on each failed night to confirm it is the same one
Look for a change on the client or its network around the first failed night
Check the error code entry for the specific cause and fix
fixes: Fix the root cause, then run a manual backup and confirm it completes
If the data has gone unprotected for several days, tell the application owner

entries.title: Missed backup: client with no job at all on a night
entries.symptoms: A client that normally runs every night has no job record for the night. Nothing failed because nothing ran.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: Schedule disabled, changed or removed
Client or agent was offline when the job window opened
Job never queued because the scheduler or a resource was unavailable
Client was decommissioned or renamed
checks: Check the client's schedule and confirm it is enabled
Check whether the client was up and reachable during the backup window
Check whether the client was recently renamed, moved or retired
fixes: Re-enable or correct the schedule, then run a catch-up backup
If the client is gone, remove it from the schedule so it stops alerting

entries.title: Silent size drop: job succeeded but backed up far less than normal
entries.symptoms: A job reports Completed but the data size is a small fraction of the client's normal. Success status hides a possible gap.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: Part of the data is no longer being included (content or filter change)
A volume, database or mount was missing or empty at backup time
Source data genuinely shrank, for example a purge or archive
checks: Compare what the job protected with what the client's content definition says it should
Ask whether the application owner purged or moved data that night
Check that all expected volumes or databases were present on the client
fixes: If content was dropped by mistake, restore the content definition and run a full backup
If the drop is expected, note it so the baseline can adjust

entries.title: Size spike: job backed up far more than normal
entries.symptoms: An incremental backup is several times larger than the client's normal, which can mean unusual change or newly included data.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: Large data load, migration or restore on the client
Content definition changed and new data was added
Application produced large temporary files or logs
Possible mass change on the client, which should be ruled out
checks: Ask the application owner whether a load, migration or batch job ran
Check whether the content definition changed recently
Check for unusual file activity on the client if no planned event explains it
fixes: Expect a longer window and more storage use; confirm capacity is available
Escalate to security if the change looks unplanned

entries.title: Duration spike: job took far longer than normal
entries.symptoms: A job finished successfully but ran many times longer than its normal duration without a matching increase in data.
entries.source: STARTER DRAFT (Claude): rewrite from your own experience or a public vendor doc, then change this source
likely_causes: Network or storage contention during the window
Slow client disk or heavy client load
Throttled or busy media agent
Many small files or retries slowing the job
checks: Check whether other jobs on the same media agent or site were slow in the same window
Check client load and disk performance during the backup window
Check network utilization between the client and the media agent
fixes: If it repeats, move the schedule or rebalance the media agent load
If it was a single occurrence, record it and watch the next night
